derivation_notes: The fixed-resistance assumption is relaxed by introducing a delayed vasomotor state driven by the same bounded baroreflex pressure error already used for heart-rate control. Choosing the new state's initial condition as zero places the system on the baseline no-effect manifold at the stated initial pressure, so the added branch is initially inactive but can recruit dynamically after perturbation.
change_summary: Systemic vascular resistance is no longer fixed during the transient; it is modulated by a finite-timescale, saturating baroreflex vasomotor state. This changes the target mapping itself because vascular outflow in dP_a_dt now depends on pressure-error history as well as current pressure and heart rate.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Systemic vascular resistance is fixed during the short pressure-perturbation experiment.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Baroreflex-mediated peripheral vasoconstriction/vasodilation with finite recruitment time, producing transient changes in effective systemic resistance alongside heart-rate control.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when reflex_resistance_gain = 0, or in the fast-relaxation/no-drive limit where R_v remains at its baseline zero-effect value.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping uses a fixed systemic_vascular_resistance, so for given P_a and H the vascular outflow term P_a/systemic_vascular_resistance is independent of current baroreflex activation and pressure error.
response_change.child_relation: Make effective vascular resistance depend on the same pressure-error-driven autonomic state that adjusts heart rate, so the pressure-to-dP_a_dt mapping changes jointly with H: during hypotensive excursions resistance rises and during hypertensive excursions it falls or relaxes toward baseline, altering outflow as an interacting reflex branch rather than a fixed environment.
response_change.observable_effect: After equal-magnitude pressure decreases versus increases from baseline, the child predicts asymmetric pressure recovery because vasoconstrictor support during low-pressure phases reduces outflow in addition to tachycardia, whereas the parent can only speed recovery through H and fixed outflow.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Most visible for pressure perturbations large enough that autonomic feedback is engaged over several heart-rate adjustment times, especially when |P_a - pressure_set_point| is a non-negligible fraction of baroreflex_saturation_pressure_scale and runoff meaningfully contributes to dP_a_dt.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training near moderate deviations, the mechanism appears as faster-than-parent recovery from hypotension relative to hypertension at similar |pressure error|; in holdout with larger excursions the same reflex-resistance interaction amplifies that asymmetry as heart-rate sensitivity saturates.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the reflex resistance modulation gain to zero, or equivalently making the added vascular-control state relax instantly to its baseline no-effect value.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A finite-timescale vascular sympathetic branch cannot be represented by refitting the fixed systemic_vascular_resistance alone, because the intended effect is dynamic and history-dependent during the transient; a state is needed to encode delayed vasomotor recruitment/relaxation.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: baroreflex vasomotor modulation of vascular runoff
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Baroreflex-mediated peripheral vasoconstriction/vasodilation with finite recruitment time, producing transient changes in effective systemic resistance alongside heart-rate control.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient correction because the target equation now depends on a delayed internal control state that is itself generated by a bounded nonlinear reflex law and enters the runoff denominator through a saturating modulation. That creates history-dependent asymmetry in the scored mapping rather than a single shared runoff slope.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Systemic vascular resistance is a fixed environment during the transient.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Systemic vascular resistance is dynamically modulated by a finite-timescale, saturating baroreflex vasomotor branch driven by pressure error.
evolution_contract.after_fragment: (stroke_volume*H/(seconds_per_minute*(1 + (H/resting_heart_rate)**2)) - P_a/(systemic_vascular_resistance*(1 + reflex_resistance_gain*R_v/(1 + Abs(R_v)))))/((arterial_compliance/(1 + arterial_stiffening_gain*P_a/(arterial_stiffening_pressure_scale + P_a)))*(1 + viscoelastic_buffering_gain*Abs(P_a - P_v)/(viscoelastic_pressure_scale + Abs(P_a - P_v))))
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Set reflex_resistance_gain = 0, or keep R_v identically zero, to recover the parent runoff law exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: For trajectories starting from the shared baseline initial condition and subjected to brief positive versus negative pressure perturbations, matched current P_a and similar H can still yield different dP_a_dt because R_v carries delayed baroreflex vasomotor recruitment. The effect is strongest when |P_a - pressure_set_point| is appreciable relative to baroreflex_saturation_pressure_scale: hypotensive recovery shows smaller runoff and faster pressure support, while hypertensive recovery shows larger runoff or weaker support.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the sign-dependent asymmetry and the recruitment lag across positive and negative perturbations, because its outflow branch is always P_a divided by one constant systemic_vascular_resistance. Adjusting baroreflex sensitivity or heart-rate timescale can reshape H, but cannot make runoff at the same P_a depend on recent pressure history or autonomic phase.

evolution_plan.promotion_reason: A finite-timescale vascular sympathetic branch cannot be represented by refitting the fixed systemic_vascular_resistance alone, because the intended effect is dynamic and history-dependent during the transient; a state is needed to encode delayed vasomotor recruitment/relaxation.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model includes baroreflex control of heart rate but treats systemic vascular resistance as fixed, omitting short-timescale autonomic vasomotor adjustment that changes vascular outflow during the same perturbation.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Stroke volume and systemic vascular resistance are fixed during the short experiment.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Baroreflex-mediated peripheral vasoconstriction/vasodilation with finite recruitment time, producing transient changes in effective systemic resistance alongside heart-rate control.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-resistance assumption rather than add an unrelated process. In the parent, varying P_a while holding the parameter set fixed changes dP_a_dt through two channels only: direct runoff P_a/systemic_vascular_resistance and the heart-rate trajectory H. Thus at matched observed P_a and H, the target slope is constrained by one fixed runoff law. In the child, pressure error also drives a vasomotor branch, so the same P_a and similar H can yield different dP_a_dt depending on whether the system is in a hypotensive recovery phase or hypertensive recovery phase and on recent pressure history. This is an actual target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary trajectory change, because effective outflow entering dP_a_dt changes. The contrast is observable after brief positive versus negative pressure perturbations from the stated initial condition, with all fixed parameters shared: the child allows stronger support of pressure during low-pressure recovery and weaker support during high-pressure recovery, creating asymmetric return dynamics and altered damping. A single parent parameter set may mimic one side by changing systemic_vascular_resistance or baroreflex sensitivity, but cannot reproduce both the sign-dependent asymmetry and the finite recruitment lag across those conditions because its outflow branch is pressure-proportional with one shared constant resistance. The mechanism is admissible on short timescales and can be turned off continuously by zero modulation gain, recovering the parent law.

scenario_text: Arterial pressure and heart rate are recorded after a brief pressure perturbation in an otherwise stable subject. The target is the rate of change of arterial pressure generated by the balance between cardiac inflow and vascular outflow, while heart rate is adjusted by pressure-sensitive autonomic feedback. Pressure and heart rate must therefore be evolved together from their initial values. The coupled negative-feedback response may return to baseline through a damped oscillation.
